ADR-0007 engine review (Godot 4.7.2, GDScript). Nothing run or edited. The engine reference has no core/IO/export module, so everything about JSON/FileAccess/export below is from my own knowledge, and I have no first-hand knowledge of 4.5-4.7 changes in those areas (treat as unverified). Confidence is in brackets.

OVERALL: The approach (manifest-listed JSON, read with FileAccess, parsed with `JSON.new().parse`, cast to typed RefCounted catalogs, injected) is idiomatic for 4.7.2 [high]. No API in it is removed or deprecated. The `FileAccess.store_*` bool change is irrelevant, as the ADR says. There are 3 blocking issues, all in details the ADR states as fact.

BLOCKING

B1. `const FIELDS: Array[FieldSpec]` (section 1.4, closed schemas) will not compile [high, ~90%].
- GDScript `const` needs a constant expression. `FieldSpec.new(...)` is an Object construction, so it is rejected ("assigned value for constant must be constant").
- Options:
  - `const` of plain literal rows (arrays/dicts of ints and strings), converted to `FieldSpec` by a `static func fields() -> Array[FieldSpec]` or by the loader.
  - A `static func` factory built per load. This needs no static state and fits "no static singleton".
- Do not use `static var`; it conflicts with the ADR's own no-static-state rule.
- Update the "schema is a code constant" wording accordingly.

B2. Packed-array exposure breaks the immutability guarantee (section 1.5, "packed arrays exposed as a copy built once") [high, ~85%].
- In GDScript, packed arrays returned by script-defined getters are shared references, not copy-on-write values. The engine docs say packed arrays are always passed by reference, and only built-in properties/methods return copies.
- A getter that returns a "copy built once" hands every caller the same mutable object. One caller's write corrupts what every later caller sees. This undermines AC-85.
- `make_read_only` does not exist on packed arrays.
- Pick one:
  - Typed `Array[int]` plus `make_read_only()`. This is safe and allocation-free per call; the cost is boxed Variants.
  - Index accessors such as `count()` and `at(i)`, exposing no container.
  - `duplicate()` per call, which allocates and violates AC-69.
- Closely related: GDScript has no private fields, so `_field` on a row object is only a convention. The "write-once" claim is enforced by lint and test, not the language. Say so.

B3. The AC-69 zero-allocation test cannot detect the failure it targets (Validation Criteria, `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.OBJECT_COUNT)`) [high].
- OBJECT_COUNT counts only `Object` instances (Node, RefCounted, Resource).
- Arrays, Dictionaries, Strings and packed arrays are Variants, not Objects, so a query that returns a fresh `duplicate()`d array leaves the delta at zero.
- The monitor is valid for "no new Objects" and for the "exactly 25 Objects" load check. That load check needs the loader and all temporaries (JSON, FileAccess, ContentRead, BootError, IntRead, FieldSpec) out of scope first.
- For the no-copy guarantee, add an identity assertion: two calls to the same accessor return the same array and `is_read_only()` is true. Use `is_same`, or compare `get_instance_id` where available.
- `IntField.read` returns an `IntRead` object per number. That is fine for boot, but it inflates Object churn, so keep it out of the 25-object accounting.

MINOR

1. Pass-by-reference of Array: if a caller assigns a read-only array into its own variable and calls `append`, it errors at runtime ("Array is in read-only state"). In release this is a printed error plus a no-op, not an exception. Tests should assert `is_read_only()` rather than rely on the error [high]. `duplicate()` returns a mutable copy [medium].

2. `var set: ContentSet` in `ContentLoadResult` [low-medium, ~50%]. `get` and `set` are GDScript property-accessor keywords and may be rejected or confusing as identifiers. Rename to `content_set`.

3. Section 1.3 says `FileAccess.get_file_as_string` has "no error channel" [medium, ~70%]. I believe it returns "" and sets `FileAccess.get_open_error()`. Your choice of `open` + `get_as_text` is still fine and gives an explicit null check. Correct the rationale.

4. BOM [low-medium].
- I am not sure whether `get_as_text()` strips a UTF-8 BOM or leaves U+FEFF for the JSON parser to reject.
- Do not assert "a leading BOM is CONTENT_JSON_PARSE" as engine behaviour. Check explicitly (`text.begins_with("\uFEFF")`) and raise your own code, or record the observed behaviour in CONTENT-EXP-1.

5. Duplicate keys inside a JSON object [high]. The parser silently keeps the last value (Dictionary overwrite), so the closed-schema pass cannot see duplicates. Add a raw-text lint, alongside `INT_LITERAL_SHAPE`. Also record in the spike how the parser treats trailing commas, comments and trailing garbage [low on the specifics].

6. Number boundary at 2^53 (section 1.4) [high]. The literal 9007199254740993 parses to 9007199254740992.0, so a `<= 2^53` check accepts a silently rounded value. Use `< 2^53` (exclusive) and also catch it in the raw-text lint. A literal above 2^53 that is exactly representable passes anyway. The wording "anything above 2^53 is CONTENT_INT_PRECISION" does not cover 2^53+1.

7. Case sensitivity [high, ~90%]. The Windows editor's `res://` is case-insensitive; the PCK and Linux/Steam Deck are case-sensitive. A manifest path with the wrong case passes in the editor and fails in the export. Add a lint that compares each manifest path with the real on-disk casing. The spike should run on the Deck, or at least on Linux.

8. CRLF [medium-high]. The JSON parser treats `\r` as whitespace, so CRLF parses. Add `.gitattributes` `*.json text eol=lf` for tidy diffs and for any raw-text lint.

9. Headless CI scripts using `class_name` [high, ~85%]. A `godot --headless -s tools/ci/content_lint.gd` run needs the global class cache, so run `godot --headless --import` (or open the editor once) first. Otherwise every `class_name` is unresolved.

10. Release export contents. Exclude `addons/gdUnit4/*` from the release preset. The ADR's `exclude_filter` list omits it.

11. DirAccess [medium]. In an export, `res://` listing goes through the PCK. Imported assets appear as `.import` or `.remap` names. Ordering is not guaranteed to match the editor. This matches the ADR's rationale, and the ADR bans scans anyway.

12. 4.7 typed-return rule [high, per the reference]. An override that omits `-> T` now inherits the base's return type. Every `ContentSource` override must `return` a `ContentRead` on all paths. The ADR's base `read_text` already does.

13. The packed-array element-write change [high, per the reference] is irrelevant, because catalogs have no setters.

14. `roundi` rounds half away from zero (negatives included). Document that for `scaled()` fields [medium-high]. `floorf` and `absf` are valid and accept the double-precision Variant float [high].

15. Presentation only: each `class_name` needs its own file. The Section 1.3 snippet puts two in one block.

CONFIRMED OK

- `JSON.new().parse(text)` returns an `Error`. Data comes from `get_data()`. `get_error_line()` and `get_error_message()` are valid after a failed parse [high]. Preferring it over `JSON.parse_string` is right, since `parse_string` returns null and prints an error that would trip gdUnit4 [medium-high]. The error message text is engine-defined, so never assert on it.
- Every JSON number parses to float (including `40000.0` and `1e9`) [high on float, ~85%]. Accepting both TYPE_INT and TYPE_FLOAT in `IntField.read` is correct hedging. Integral doubles are exact up to 2^53 [certain]. Reject `true`/`false` explicitly (TYPE_BOOL).
- `FileAccess.open` returns null on failure, with `FileAccess.get_open_error()` as a static call [high]. `get_as_text()` works [high]. `FileAccess.open("res://...")` reads any file that is in the PCK, including a template_release export [high]. File reads are not remapped.
- A `.json` file needs `include_filter` to be exported [high, ~90%]. By default "export all resources" does not copy non-resource files; this is the documented "export non-resource files" behaviour. The files are copied raw, with no import or remap, so the `ResourceLoader` fallback is probably never needed [medium, ~75%]. `JSON` is also a Resource type, but that is not relevant to your path.
- Glob syntax [medium-high, ~75%]:
  - `include_filter` and `exclude_filter` are comma-separated globs.
  - The editor matches each against the full `res://` path, the path without `res://`, and the file name.
  - `matchn` is case-insensitive and `*` matches `/`. So `assets/data/*.json` or plain `*.json` hits nested files, and `tests/*` excludes the whole folder.
  - For `EXPORT_FILTER_MISSES_MANIFEST`, reuse `String.matchn` with the same three-way path test rather than a re-implementation.
- `Array.make_read_only()` works on typed `Array[ItemDef]` [high]. A getter returning the stored array returns the same reference each call, with no allocation [high]. `Dictionary.make_read_only()` is shallow [high]. A typed `Dictionary[String, ...]` is valid in 4.7 (typed dictionaries since 4.4) [high].
- `static func` in a `class_name ... extends RefCounted` with no static state is fine. A `Variant` parameter with `typeof()` branches is fine.
- `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.OBJECT_COUNT)` exists and works in release builds [high]. It is valid only as an Object-count check (see B3).
- `--headless` works in template_release binaries [medium-high], so the exported-build smoke check is feasible.

Relevant file: D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\docs\architecture\adr-0007-static-content-data-pipeline-and-stable-type-ids.md (sections 1.3-1.6 and Key Interfaces).
